description: The pie chart presents the distribution of cited or referenced media sources in the context of “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” showing 17 slices (categories) labeled around the circle, with numeric values printed inside each slice. The largest slice is “Breitbart” in dark blue at approximately 14, followed by “Other” in dark gray at approximately 13. Mid-sized slices include “Drudge Report” in brown at about 8 and “The Daily Caller” in green at about 8, then “The Huffington Post” in dark red at about 7. Two similarly sized slices, “NPR” (purple) and “Vox” (brownish) are each about 6, followed by “The Guardian” (mauve) and “BBC” (purple) at about 5 each, and “RT” (olive) at about 4. Smaller slices include “Daily Kos” (teal) and “National Review” (blue-green) at about 3 each, plus several additional slices at about 3 each—“Daily Mail” (orange), “RedState” (green), “Fox News” (red), “CNN” (purple), “PoliticusUSA” (brown), and “Shareblue” (pink). There is no separate legend; labels are placed around the pie, and the slice values appear inside the segments, with no slices visibly exploded or otherwise emphasized; the segments do not appear strictly ordered by size around the circle.
